title: A tree of four leaves, and the nodes under its root
request:
four leaves, then the root and one node from each level

./your_program.sh merkle
build t a,b,c,d
root t
node t 0 0
node t 1 0
node t 2 0
note: Level 0 is the leaves and the top level holds the single root, so `node t 2 0` and `root t` are the same string. `node t 0 0` is sha256(0x00 || "a") and nothing else: the 0x00 is what stops a leaf from ever colliding with a node.

title: Three leaves, and the one that is carried up
request:
an odd tree, then the lone node at level 1 and the leaf it came from

./your_program.sh merkle
build o a,b,c
node o 1 1
node o 0 2
root o
note: `c` has no sibling, so it rises to level 1 untouched. Hashing it with itself instead would be the other obvious rule and gives a different root — and it is the rule behind the CVE-2012-2459 duplicate-transaction bug in Bitcoin, where two different leaf lists hash to the same tree.
